alt.en: A yellowed book page numbered 119 and headed "ABIDE WITH ME." Under the heading comes the verse "Abide with us: for it is towards evening, and the day is far spent." St. Luke xxiv. 29, then the first two verses of the hymn, beginning "Abide with me! Fast falls the eventide;", and the first two lines of the third. There is no music.
alt.es: Página amarillenta de un libro, numerada 119 y con el encabezado "ABIDE WITH ME." Bajo el encabezado va el versículo "Abide with us: for it is towards evening, and the day is far spent." St. Luke xxiv. 29, y después las dos primeras estrofas del himno, que empiezan "Abide with me! Fast falls the eventide;", y los dos primeros versos de la tercera. No hay música.

caption.en: Abide with Me as it opens in Lyte's Remains (London, 1850), the book that printed all eight of his verses, without music, under Luke 24:29.
caption.es: Abide with Me tal como empieza en los Remains de Lyte (Londres, 1850), el libro que imprimió sus ocho estrofas, sin música, bajo Lucas 24:29.

source: Remains of the late Rev. Henry Francis Lyte, M.A., incumbent of Lower Brixham, Devon; with a prefatory memoir (London: Francis & John Rivington, 1850), p. 119, "Abide with me"

alt.en: A page of printed music headed "Evening." and "Hymn 14." Three systems of two staves, treble and bass, with three flats in the key signature, written mostly in long notes, end with the word "A-men." There are no words under the notes. A small pencil tick is at the top.
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el encabezado "Evening." y "Hymn 14." Tres sistemas de dos pentagramas, en clave de sol y de fa, con tres bemoles en la armadura y notas largas en su mayoría, terminan con la palabra "A-men." No hay letra bajo las notas. Arriba hay una pequeña marca a lápiz.

caption.en: Monk's tune for Abide with Me, now called EVENTIDE, as Hymns Ancient and Modern printed it in 1861, the year the tune came out: Hymn 14, among the evening hymns, with Lyte's words on the next page.
caption.es: La melodía de Monk para Abide with Me, hoy llamada EVENTIDE, tal como la imprimió Hymns Ancient and Modern en 1861, el año en que salió la melodía: el himno 14, entre los himnos de la tarde, con la letra de Lyte en la página siguiente.

source: Hymns Ancient and Modern, for use in the services of the Church, with accompanying tunes, musical editor William Henry Monk (London: Novello, 1861), Hymn 14, "Evening"
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)

alt.en: A yellowed book page headed "ABIDE WITH ME." and numbered 121, with the hymn's last two verses, from "I fear no foe with Thee at hand to bless:" to "In life and death, O Lord, abide with me!", and under them, in italics, "Berryhead, September, 1847." The lower half of the page is blank.
alt.es: Página amarillenta de un libro con el encabezado "ABIDE WITH ME." y el número 121, con las dos últimas estrofas del himno, desde "I fear no foe with Thee at hand to bless:" hasta "In life and death, O Lord, abide with me!", y debajo, en cursiva, "Berryhead, September, 1847." La mitad de abajo de la página está en blanco.

caption.en: The close of the hymn in the Remains (1850), signed "Berryhead, September, 1847", though a letter Lyte sent from Berry Head on 25 August already enclosed it.
caption.es: El final del himno en los Remains (1850), firmado "Berryhead, September, 1847", aunque una carta que Lyte envió desde Berry Head el 25 de agosto ya lo incluía.
